Edit #1 (2 hr mark): I made 2 different motor shields,  one to allow for one motor, and another to allow for another motor. While making the first motor shield, i was thinking of how to allow for 2 motors to go off the same board, but i couldnt figure out how to make the schematic for that. I decided to remove some pins from the r3 to allow for it, as in pin 7 and pin 4 for the singular motor, motor driver. then i had to figure out whether to put a heatsink, but i decided against it as there would be no space to place one. In the first 2 images shown, my issues were the tolerances, as i wasnt exactly sure if putting sockets on the opposite side of the arduino, would allow for the arduino to fit. For the other one, it was my progress at the 1.5hr ish mark, i was still researching how motor shields work.
![image_2026-10-11_203632274](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ICfGl9WlsUCo0vTQqywfbnXlt0PfIwC1/610167095e6afc459e822e38408ee3bf2d15341cce45f2df07a620d951cb2163.png)
Edit#2 (5.5 hr mark): I finally figured out how to make it so there would be 1 motor, and 2 motors both accepted. After doing some in-depth research in arduino chips, and how motor drivers work. I decided to remove 4 pins from the arduino uno r3, and just internally attach them to the inputs for the motors. This theoretically should allow for 2 motors, but 4 less pins, which im planning to fix soon, possibly? deadlines is soon so I will ship this version, as itll still allow for a ton of pins to be used. I ended up switching pins 7 and 4 with 5 and  6 after finding out that the motor driver only works with pins that allow PWM, which messed up some stuff for me which i later fixed.

![image_2026-10-11_233953306](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ICfGl9WlsUCo0vTQqywfbnXlt0PfIwC1/13adafab901ac39d232d2459c4afeedef8fa0510d3c2d546d7354a4e39e5f5be.png)

![image_2026-10-11_233911689](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ICfGl9WlsUCo0vTQqywfbnXlt0PfIwC1/f32ccfd3103ca3164e4c8178aa8bf48ca98d5751e06509effe61705f9c6c6404.png)

The PCB routing was a bit challenging with the amount of pins that i needed to connect, so i ended up using a ton of vias. I also found out that connecting the vcc pin of the motor driver to the arduino will probably fry the arduino, so i decided to keep that pin, and just internally connect the ground of motor driver to the ground of arduino.
